title: Coverage ratio stress tests + headcount shift scenarios
summary: Ad-hoc financial sheet to run coverage ratio and runway sensitivity across pricing and headcount phasing options; includes manual calculations, triggers, and recommended near-term actions.
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet lays out a compact set of scenarios to test how price changes and shifts in hiring cadence (headcount phasing) affect revenue coverage ratios, gross margin per FTE, and runway. Intended for CFO + FP&A review ahead of the Q4 hiring cadence decision.

Key outputs (one-pagers we expect to extract):
- Coverage ratio (Revenue / Fully-loaded labor cost) across scenarios
- Months of runway delta under each sensitivity case
- Marginal contribution per new SWE/SRE/CS hire at different price points
- Trigger rules for accelerating or pausing hires

Top-line assumptions (base case):
- Annual recurring revenue (ARR) current run-rate: $72.0M (as of 2025-07)
- Monthly revenue recognition for modeling: $6.0M
- Average fully-loaded cost per head (blended across roles): $180k/year ($15k/mo)
- Current headcount (finance view): 400 FTEs total; finance model uses 260 engineering + infra + SRE + 140 GTM + support/ops distributed
- Gross margin (inference unit margin after infra costs but before labor): 58%
- Base price per 1k tokens (effective to Redwood after discounts/commits): $0.014 per 1k tokens
- Baseline monthly token volume growth: +3.5% month-over-month

Scenario matrix (primary levers):
- Price changes: Base (0%), +8% uplift (price test), -12% downside (competitive pressure)
- Headcount phasing: On-track hiring (baseline: +40 hires over next 6 months), Delay hires (pause 50% of planned hires for 3 months), Accelerate (front-load +20 hires in next 2 months)
- Labor mix tilt: Standard (60% eng, 40% GTM/support) vs. Eng-heavy (70% eng) vs. GTM-heavy (55% eng)

Manual sensitivity snapshots (summary numbers rounded):
Baseline (no price change, on-track hires):
- Revenue/mo: $6.0M
- Monthly labor run-rate (fully-loaded): 400 * $15k = $6.0M
- Coverage ratio (Revenue / Labor) = 1.00
- Months runway impact if net burn increases by 5%: -1.8 months on existing runway estimate

Upside (+8% price, on-track hires):
- Revenue/mo = $6.0M * 1.08 = $6.48M
- Coverage ratio = 6.48 / 6.0 = 1.08 (+8 percentage points)
- Incremental gross (pre-labor) uplift captured: assume 70% flows to gross margin = ~$336k/mo extra for every $400k extra revenue
- Effective marginal contribution per new SWE (full-stack) at scale = ~$6.6k/mo incremental revenue required to keep coverage flat (back-solved)

Downside (-12% price, on-track hires):
- Revenue/mo = $6.0M * 0.88 = $5.28M
- Coverage ratio = 5.28 / 6.0 = 0.88 (coverage breach)
- To restore to coverage >=1.0 without changing price, reduce labor run-rate to 5.28M => need headcount reduction of ~48 FTEs (48*$15k = $720k annualized reduction equals $60k/mo) — note: headcount reductions have cost/impact beyond modeling (severance, product velocity)

Headcount shift sensitivities (price constant at base):
- Delay hires (pause 20 hires for 3 months): immediate labor run-rate reduction = 20*$15k = $300k/mo => Coverage ratio improves to (6.0 / (6.0 - 0.3)) = 1.05
- Accelerate hires (+20 now): labor +$300k/mo; coverage falls to 0.95. If accelerated hires lead to faster revenue recognition (assume +1.5% revenue/mo for two months) net effect moderates to ~0.98

Labor mix impact (baseline revenue):
- Eng-heavy hiring raises average fully-loaded head cost (senior mix) to $195k/year => labor run-rate +$65k/mo for 10 hires shift; coverage drops ~1.1 percentage points.
- GTM-heavy (more sales/CS) tends to increase revenue per incremental hire but with longer ramp; short-term coverage can worsen despite positive long-term payback.

Action triggers (operational rules tied to finance signals):
- If trailing-3mo actual price realization falls >7% vs plan => pause non-critical hires for 60 days and trigger pricing response with Growth/Product by Ticket PR-PRC-005
- If coverage ratio <0.92 for two consecutive months => immediate hiring freeze + targeted expense review (SaaS contracts, travel)
- If price test (+8%) maintains >4% incremental gross margin for 90 days => resume hires and re-evaluate compensation/bonus pools to attract senior hires

Recommended near-term plan (finance + talent ops):
- Contingency: Pre-approve a 30-day hiring buffer fund equal to $900k to enable strategic hiring bursts if price test performs well
- Phasing: Move 60% of planned Q4 engineering openings to H1 FY26 and accelerate 40% of GTM early hires if price holds
- Reporting cadence: Weekly coverage-ratio snapshot to CFO, FP&A, and Talent Ops until coverage ratio stable above 1.05 for two months

Open questions / risks (notes to reviewer):
- Model assumes linear revenue lift when accelerating GTM; real-world ramp is heteroskedastic — need funnel-level inputs from growth
- Severance and rehiring costs are not captured; run a scenario including 1.2x rehiring friction and one-time separation costs of $5k/head where applicable
- Quantization of infrastructure savings (e.g., batching/optimize) could improve coverage without headcount changes — coordinate with Applied ML for potential $/token savings

Next steps / owners:
- FP&A to convert this sheet into a detailed per-role months-of-ramp model (owner: Priya Desai) — due 2025-08-28
- Talent Ops to produce a 6-month candidate pipeline and estimate time-to-hire per role (owner: Marco Ruiz) — due 2025-08-22
- Growth/Product to run a controlled price test on a subset of accounts and report delta revenue capture monthly (owner: Liam O'Connor) — test window 2025-08-15 to 2025-11-15

Notes to self / working items: 
- Insert granular table: per-role fully-loaded cost, expected ramp %, and expected revenue uplift by month (WIP tab)
- Validate token unit economics with serving/runtime team: are we capturing edge-case infra credits and committed capacity discounts?

End of sheet.
